findings.message: FR-009 says that after the story, a case-insensitive search for `resource[ _]?type` in backend/src finds only the historical migration files of earlier stories and their designer files. This new acceptance-test file still has one hit, in a doc comment. The comment itself claims the opposite: that the old names are built by concatenation so the search finds nothing in this file. No other file outside the migrations matches, and no production code or user-visible text is affected. Severity is MINOR, not BLOCKER, because FR-009 is a functional requirement and not an AC, decision or contract clause (AC-6, AC-7 and AC-13 do not cover test source). The file is a hashed acceptance-test file (red-first), so fixing it requires a rebaseline decision like DEC-7. Side note on the same rule: the story's own migration (20261007131957_RenameResourceTypeToResourceSchema.cs and its Designer) has to contain the old names in order to rename them. FR-009 as written ('earlier stories' only) does not allow for that. This is a gap in the spec text, not a code defect; the owner should widen FR-009 to include this story's migration.
findings.evidence: ResourcesApiDescriptionTests.cs:29: `/// the old name (FR-009) finds no hit in this file. "resource type" also covers "resource types";` (Grep `(?i)resource[ _]?type` over backend/src: hits only in Migrations/* and this line)
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the comment so it does not contain the old phrase. Apply this through the acceptance-test rebaseline path, because the file is hashed.

findings.message: A table rename in the Resources module forced edits in the ManagementGroups test project: it reads resources.resource_schemas with raw SQL (ManagementGroupsTestClient.cs:128) and seeds schemas and instances through the public Resources API (DeleteManagementGroupTests.cs:89, :100, :114). Both lines were edited here. It is test-only and may be deliberate for the cascade test, so this is an owner decision rather than a violation. Constitution IV forbids a module from querying another module's database; this is a test project, not a module.
findings.evidence: ManagementGroupsTestClient.cs:128: `"""SELECT COUNT(1) FROM resources.resource_schemas WHERE "GroupId" = @groupId"""`; DeleteManagementGroupTests.cs:89: `owner.Client.PostAsJsonAsync("/resources/schemas", new`
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: keep the cross-module cascade check, but isolate the Resources table name and routes in one helper so the next Resources rename touches one place.

findings.message: The diff introduces near-identical test scaffolding and overlapping coverage. MemberAccessBaselineTests and OutsiderAccessBaselineTests each define their own `Baseline` record and `SeedAsync` with the same schema, definition, instance and value seeding, differing only in names. ForeignSchemaFilterTests seeds the same shape again. Several 'missing id' and 'only owner may' cases are asserted three times (Member rows 6/8/10/13, Outsider rows 6/8/10/13, ResourceSchemaMessagesTests). The two 409 tests in ResourceSchemaContractTests repeat CreateResourceSchemaEndpointTests.CreateResourceSchema_DuplicateNameInGroup_Returns409 and UpdateResourceSchemaEndpointTests.UpdateResourceSchema_DuplicateAmongOthers_Returns409, which this diff also extended with AC-1 and AC-7 traits and the same code and message assertions.
findings.evidence: MemberAccessBaselineTests.cs:55 `private async Task<Baseline> SeedAsync(string prefix)` vs OutsiderAccessBaselineTests.cs:70 `private async Task<Baseline> SeedAsync(string prefix)`; ResourceSchemaContractTests `CreateResourceSchema_WithTakenName_Returns409WithSchemaNameTakenCode` vs CreateResourceSchemaEndpointTests `CreateResourceSchema_DuplicateNameInGroup_Returns409`
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a shared seeding helper (a factory-style class in Clients/) and drop or merge the duplicated 409 and missing-id tests, keeping one test per (AC, behaviour).

The knowledge of the old names is duplicated and the obfuscation makes the tests harder to read. A path allowlist in the FR-009 check would be simpler.

findings.message: Regenerating the API client brought unrelated churn into a story that only renames Resources. In ManagementGroups.ts the nullable query types changed (`string | null` became `string`, `query` became optional), the error type changed from `any` to ProblemDetails, and `addGroupMember` was moved. In data-contracts.ts interfaces were reordered and a ProblemDetails type was added. This hides the real rename in review and changes ManagementGroups call signatures with no AC behind it.
findings.evidence: ManagementGroups.ts:14 `+  MicrosoftAspNetCoreMvcProblemDetails,` ; diff: `-    query: {\n-      name?: string | null;` / `+    query?: {\n+      name?: string;` ; `-      any` / `+      MicrosoftAspNetCoreMvcProblemDetails`
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate against the same generator version/config as main, or revert the hunks unrelated to resourceSchemaId / resources/schemas, so the diff of generated files contains only the rename.

findings.message: The spec is written to compile 'before and after the rename': it finds the service class by scanning module exports, calls methods by string name, and guesses the create-instance method with a regex. Now that the rename is done this reflection layer is dead flexibility. It hides typos behind run-time errors and loses type checking of the payloads.
findings.evidence: resources-api.service.spec.ts:25 `function findServiceClass(): Type<unknown> {` ... `const service = candidates.find((c) => /Service$/.test(c.name)) ?? candidates[0];` ; :134 `const createInstance = methodNames(service).find((n) => /^create/i.test(n) && !/schema/i.test(n));`
findings.suggested_fix: Inject ResourcesApiService directly and call getResourceSchemas / createResourceSchema / createResourceInstance with typed arguments.
